capabilities.truth_boundary: Standalone Simics fixture TV-audio passthrough and receiver DMA suite; exported AuroraSim integration pending. Does not implement a TV OS, Netflix application, DRM or physical eARC discovery/signalling.
Standalone ideal 24-bit DAC and resistive-load model fed by actual Simics DMA output; exported AuroraSim integration pending. No vendor DAC, amplifier, acoustic model or physical speaker measurement.

Standalone Simics 7.84.0 vacuum harness passes 21 profiles including MMIO/DMA timing, full DSP PCM replay and MCHStreamer/UAC2 transport-contract checks. Export into AuroraSim capability mapping is still pending; no guest driver, vendor register accuracy or physical electrical timing is proven.

Software Gate A-Live has bounded retained diagnostics, threshold-driven pass/fail verdicts and Linux/Windows self-tests for mid-stream acquisition and relock. Export into AuroraSim remains pending; physical live eARC capture, hardware reset/drop counters and electrical timing remain unproven.

Pinned Harletty JOC software is exercised through Aurora's hardware-neutral StreamingDecoder contract with explicit object-to-PCM-channel bindings, bounded priming/fault policy, bed routing, object gain rendering and speaker PCM mixing. In-process decoder panics are isolated on the media/control side, latched fail-closed across ordinary discontinuities, and require explicit recovery before a fresh priming epoch. Plain E-AC-3 is a fail-closed negative control. This is software-reference evidence only; it does not prove physical eARC capture, protected-service compatibility, final renderer quality, or Dolby certification.

Deterministic software-only coverage for Aurora-owned network transport lifecycle, exact PCM/timestamp identity, bounded overflow behavior, format-drift rejection and callback-to-worker timestamp continuity. It does not prove packets on a real network, RF loss behavior, peer clock quality, AVB/PTP hardware timestamps, AOO/GenAVB interoperability, multi-speaker physical sync or measured latency.

Focused 48 kHz stereo object-position/gain differential against exact pinned AOMedia OAR 1.0.0. Covers finite output, 256-frame accounting, FL/FR order, left/center/right semantics and -6 dB gain only; does not prove IAMF ingestion/decoding, multichannel differential equivalence, physical output or certification.

Focused 48 kHz 5.1 point-object differential against exact pinned AOMedia OAR 1.0.0. Covers explicit FL/FR/FC/LFE/SL/SR order, finite output, 256-frame accounting, exact speaker-target cases, -6 dB gain and exclusion of point-object energy from LFE. It does not prove IAMF ingestion/decoding, arbitrary trajectories, height rendering, 7.1.4 equivalence, physical output or certification.

Pinned libiamf iamfdec is built from commit e55e1832a608affe602de2ee39929bd7759a75ab and exercised on an official iamf-tools fixture. The reference lane proves real complete-file IAMF decoding to 48 kHz rendered ChannelPcm and bit-exact Aurora import after the declared PCM32-to-F32 normalization. It intentionally fabricates no objects. It does not expose or prove IAMF source-object metadata, object-to-PCM bindings, streaming IAMF, Aurora-side 7.1.4/elevation/HOA rendering, physical output, protected-service compatibility, or certification.

Pinned iamf-tools encodes hash-checked upstream stereo inputs and decodes a PCM baseline. The same generated Opus IAMF file is decoded by iamf-tools and libiamf to finite non-silent stereo 48 kHz PCM with exactly 24000 frames each. Energy and correlation are recorded, not general renderer-equivalence gates. No 5.1 downmix, object-scene ingestion, streaming, hardware or certification claim.

Aurora has executable complete-file IAMF decoding into rendered ChannelPcm and independent OAR-vs-Aurora stereo/5.1 object-renderer differentials. These remain separate reference lanes. IAMF bitstream-to-Aurora object-scene integration remains unproven until a reviewed backend exposes source object/audio-element metadata and complete object-to-PCM bindings.
Aurora has no proven Higher-Order Ambisonics scene-rendering lane; OAR supports scene-based elements up to fourth order and remains the external reference candidate.
EAR/libear differential reference lane is not yet implemented.

Executable software/reference coverage now includes explicit tracker-clock anchoring, bounded timestamp-to-media-frame mapping, stable object identity, exact-boundary HRTF scheduling, deterministic healthy/jitter delivery, burst loss, reorder, duplicate sequence, timestamp jump, stale hold and explicit reconnect/re-anchor recovery through AuroraSim. The reconnect path resets mapper and scheduler pose epochs without resetting Aurora media time or filter generation. Exact-pinned sofar remains the FIR reference lane. No physical tracker, sensor calibration, OS/radio latency, personalized HRTF, perception, acoustic output or measured motion-to-sound latency is proven.
Aurora does not yet provide a codec-neutral authored audio-element/group timeline with bounded user personalization, deterministic mix presentations, and gain/position interpolation.

Aurora represents custom speaker geometry but has no proven end-to-end layout-negotiation, speaker-loss/degraded-layout, or automatic placement-adaptation policy comparable in product goal to flexible-layout systems.
Aurora output DSP has explicit headroom and a linked limiter, but no proven BS.1770/EBU-style loudness measurement/normalization layer.

Executable virtual evidence drives Aurora's fixed-storage PPM estimator, slew-limited DriftController feed-forward and RubatoAsrc path for both +250 ppm and -250 ppm over a simulated 24 hours while keeping a fixed-capacity ring bounded. Jitter filtering, bounded correction slew, discontinuity/reacquisition and out-of-range fail-closed behavior are exercised. This does not constitute physical clock measurement or prove a specific USB/TDM/audio device.

Executable virtual evidence drives Aurora's DuplexStateMachine through bounded exponential recovery backoff, successful late reappearance, stable-run history reset, fail-closed exhaustion and flapping-device history retention. Backend reopen timing and physical device hotplug remain unproven.

Deterministic software-reference coverage for RoomEQ 7.1.4 synthetic optimization, PR-eligible LFE/sub topologies, multi-seat phase guards and Stage 3 safety-policy plumbing. The workflow emits healthy evidence plus corrupted-multichannel and contract-pin-mismatch fail-closed controls. This is not microphone/acoustic evidence, listening evidence, measured physical headroom/latency, RoomEQ-to-CamillaDSP execution fidelity, or proof of MIMO/SIMO room-field control.

Deterministic external software execution coverage for the declared RoomEQ-to-exact-pinned-CamillaDSP PCM contract subset plus Aurora's role-aware real 7.1.4 WAV channel sentinel. Includes fail-closed unsupported-plugin and corrupted-backend controls. It does not prove arbitrary DSP graphs, physical DAC/speaker wiring, acoustic room correction, measured latency or certification.
No MIMO/SIMO multi-speaker low-frequency field-control optimizer has been implemented; the covered synthetic RoomEQ reference lane is narrower and does not establish this capability.
Requires real hardware capture evidence under issue #143; no host, MCU, eARC bridge or other hardware choice is fixed by the software architecture.
Virtual multichannel transport contracts do not prove any specific USB/TDM implementation, electrical timing or clock behavior. Hardware remains intentionally unselected.
Requires a future selected output implementation and electrical/loopback measurement; Aurora software does not currently select a DAC architecture.
Synthetic measurement/calibration does not prove room response, bass field control, or multi-seat performance.
Legitimate protected-service compatibility must be tested separately without DRM circumvention.
Software, simulation and physical prototype evidence do not constitute Dolby certification or conformance.
